project_scope.note: Built around bark, bud/petiole architecture, and the many-achene spherical fruiting head.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with mottled exfoliating bark and huge alternate palmately lobed leaves, then inspect the petiole base and spherical fruiting heads.
family_diagnostics.twig: The swollen petiole base encloses the axillary bud; stipules leave an encircling scar.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Unisexual male and female flowers occur in separate spherical heads.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A persistent sphere packed with many individual achenes, not one fruit.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Alternate leaves + enclosed bud + spherical achene heads separate sycamore from maple and sweetgum.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Sycamore is visually loud, but the best lesson is that its hanging brown ball is a whole head of many achenes, not one fruit.

steps.title: 1 · See the whole sycamore architecture
steps.image_credit: Public Domain · Michaux / North American Sylva
steps.look_for: Large alternate palmately lobed leaves, mottled trunk, and hanging spherical heads.
steps.why_it_matters: Combines the family's main field cues in one view.

steps.title: 2 · Learn the bark gestalt
steps.look_for: Patchy exfoliating bark exposing pale white/cream/greenish areas.

steps.title: 3 · Find the hidden bud
steps.look_for: The swollen petiole base covers the bud until leaf fall; the stipule leaves a ring-like scar.
steps.why_it_matters: This is an excellent twig-level Platanus confirmation.

steps.title: 4 · Break apart the fruiting ball mentally
steps.look_for: A spherical head composed of many separate hairy achenes.
steps.why_it_matters: Stops the common mistake of calling the whole sphere one fruit.

comparisons.title: Platanaceae vs Acer
comparisons.rule: Sycamore leaves are alternate and fruit is a spherical achene head; maples are opposite and make paired samaras.

comparisons.title: Platanaceae vs Liquidambar
comparisons.rule: Sweetgum has woody spiny capsule balls; sycamore has softer heads of many hairy achenes.

visual_lesson.caveat: Mottled bark alone is supporting evidence; younger trunks can be darker and less dramatic.
